newsitem.title: INDIA: India starts branded flower exports,roses to France.
newsitem.headline: India starts branded flower exports,roses to France.

text.p: India's floriculture industry launched branded export of flowers on Friday with an air shipment of nearly 40,000 stems of roses to France, a senior industry official said.

"This is the first commercial branded shipment from India," Karuturi Ramakrishna of the South India Floriculture Association (SIFA), told Reuters at Bangalore, home to a fledgling flower export industry aiming for big global growth.

The state-run Karnataka Agro Industries Corporation (KAIC) coordinated the export under its brand name, Nandi, to help local rose growers reap the advantage of big shipments and a brand image, a KAIC official said at the airport.
A bigger consignment of 160,000 stems of roses was scheduled to be sent to France next Tuesday, the official said.
Each stem fetches around 10 rupees (28 U.S. cents) in the global market.

Apart from giving Indian flowers a brand image, larger consignments, usually in excess of 200,000 stems per shipment, can fetch attractive prices from bulk buyers interested in steady supplies, industry officials say.
Indian growers launched floricultural exports under an economic reform programme launched in 1991, which liberalised export of agricultural exports earlier limited by government controls.
Industry officials say India can grab a big chunk of a $40 billion global market in floricultural trade, of which roses are said to account for nearly $8.0 billion.

They say Bangalore, which has a climate conducive to grow roses for most of the year and labour cost advantages, can be a key global centre for export of roses and compete with Israel and Kenya, which currently feed a huge European demand.
The demand peaks during European winters, when local production slumps.

Bangalore's exporters sold in excess of $10 million worth roses in 1996/97 (April-March), but this is described as just a beginning. Industry officials say poor infrastructure has created obstacles, but barriers are fast crumbling. ($1=35.8 rupees)
